my_ruling: Soft amber lights reflect off of polished brass fixtures and the soft sheen of well oiled leather gives the room the distinguished glow of aristocratic excess. It gives the rich rosewood interior of the Pall Mall Reform club a sense of sincere warmth that is a stark contrast to the world outside. Earth toned stained glass separates the rooms and burgundy leather with PC1 button seats adorn every table within. A sign over the conservatory reads “Tir Na Nog Expedition, Sign in here”. A man dressed in the manner of a fine servant such as a butler or a man servant attends a crushed velvet rope. There is a line forming to gain entrance to the room. The smell of juniper berry gin, warm brandy and rich tobacco flood your senses. The storied history of this place seems disturbed as the odd assortment of colonists arrive to sign up for passage to the new world.

my_ruling: A member of the Order of Kairo gets up to make an announcement that includes but is not limited to the following information. Upon their agreement, passage of 500 gold must be paid by the end of week one. Those who cannot or do not want to pay their own passage may have one of the four patron groups sponsor their place. Sponsorship comes with a form of employment. The patron may call upon that group of players from time to time to complete quests. A representative of each of the four patron groups will be available to take interviews and describe their beliefs and goals to their potential groups.

source_line: "The end of this week! We will bid London adieu!"
my_ruling: A delegate from the Order of Kairo: "Ladies and Gentlemen, when my journey began, I was living in an ordinary world. I was an Ordinary person without much in my pockets but a dream. Do you remember this dream? The dream of a British Empire upon which the sun would never set? This dream sailed through my dreams, and it was like a call to see the world. A call I thought I could heed. But these long 20 years, as you well know, have been filled with a doldrum of progress. The Atlantic is uncrossable by conventional means. A blockade of monstrously gigantic creatures, each able to summon forth the power of an iceberg seemingly at will. Well folks, I will level with you… it's a call I considered refusing, but my mentor told me that if I want something bad enough, I have to fight for it, you have to think around it! Now, several waiters will begin passing out glasses of champagne, so please refrain from drinking it until the end. Now where was I? Ah yes... So I did! I Fought for it, and I thought “around” the problem. Now, many of you have already heard the rumors of our… unconventional travel method. And believe you me, there were plenty of sailors who told me that what I wanted to do was impossible. That every ship that has attempted the journey in two decades has failed. But, then, in the black woods of Bavaria I discovered a gnomish inventor. He had been working on just the thing we needed. A ship that does not sail through the sea, but rather UNDER IT.

source_line: "The ship is going underwater?"
my_ruling: Be amazed as I was at his marvelous invention. For the first time in twenty long years we shall approach the shores of Arcania and reestablish what has long been lost. FOR KING AND COUNTRY I SAY! Now, I could not be standing before you today if such a venture had not been vetted by some very clever and powerful people. These people are here with us today and are here to help recruit and fund the best we can find to send back to the New World. I thank you for your time and your bravery, your ambition and your skill. We will need the best, the bravest, the smartest and the most resourceful men and women of this kingdom and all the kingdom of the Old World to succeed. Looking around this room, I have every confidence. Now, I see that you all have you glasses. Please raise them with me and stand. TO OUR JOURNEY. TO ROANOKE. Hip hip… HOORAY. Hip hip… HOORAY."

my_ruling: You attempt to reshape another creature's memories. One creature that you can see must make a Wisdom saving throw. If you are fighting the creature, it has advantage on the saving throw. On a failed save, the target becomes Charmed by you for the Duration. The Charmed target is Incapacitated and unaware of its surroundings, though it can still hear you. If it takes any damage or is targeted by another spell, this spell ends, and none of the target's memories are modified. While this charm lasts, you can affect the target's memory of an event that it experienced within the last 24 hours and that lasted no more than 10 minutes. You can permanently eliminate all memory of the event, allow the target to recall the event with perfect clarity and exacting detail, change its memory of the details of the event, or create a memory of some other event. You must speak to the target to describe how its memories are affected, and it must be able to understand your language for the modified memories to take root. Its mind fills in any gaps in the details of your description. If the spell ends before you have finished describing the modified memories, the creature's memory isn't altered. Otherwise, the modified memories take hold when the spell ends. A modified memory doesn't necessarily affect how a creature behaves, particularly if the memory contradicts the creature's natural inclinations, Alignment, or beliefs. An illogical modified memory, such as implanting a memory of how much the creature enjoyed dousing itself in acid, is dismissed, perhaps as a bad dream. The DM might deem a modified memory too nonsensical to affect a creature in a significant manner.

You are no longer proficient in it. 66-75 – The madness has crept into your subconscious and you have awful night terrors when you sleep. Whenever you take a long rest, roll a d6. On a 1, you do not gain the benefits of a long rest. This includes regaining lost HP, regaining spell slots and any abilities that reset. You do however recover HD, and can switch out spells. 76-85 – The madness has severely distorted your perception of reality. You are no longer sure of what is real and fake. You have disadvantage on all Perception rolls. 86-90 – Your spirit has been broken in some way and you are now more susceptible to danger. Roll a d6 (1=STR, 2=DEX, 3=CON, 4=INT, 5=WIS, 6=CHA). Whichever you roll, reduce that Saving Throw by 1. 91-95 – The madness you’ve experienced has caused you to lose the edge on many of things you were highly trained in. Reduce your proficiency bonus by 1. 96-99 – You have been severely touched by the madness of the Underdark. Roll a d6 and a d2. The d6 determines which stat is affected (see above) and the d2 determines how many points of that stat you lose. 100 – You completely lose your mind and fall unconscious, your mind a slave to one of the Demon Lords. While you aren’t dead, you are far from alive and nothing short of a Greater Restoration spell can break your catatonia. Even if/when you awake, you still suffer the stat and proficiency loss from above.

my_ruling: @everyone I'd like to invite you to welcome the challenges of week 4. Where last week was a chance to explore a little bit of the Island Week 4 is where you are, like all downtrodden in stories of fiction, tested the most. It will take co-operation and finding a sense of resolve in your characters. Of standing up to the problems of a neutral war torn island. There will be delicate political struggles, and chances to be brave. Loss has stricken us all. And this is not BFDM warning the players of more mental anguish. The island is a 3 act play. The second act is always the most fraught with challenge. How you deal with it is yours to choose. But for the sake of your arc and the characters you care for, band together, play smart and careful. People and places are not safe on their own. But where you are all together, you can maintain hope. I love you all. Please, maybe consider resolve as a part of your arc.

my_ruling: An immobile, invisible, cube-shaped prison composed of magical force springs into existence around an area you choose within range. The prison can be a cage or a solid box, as you choose. A prison in the shape of a cage can be up to 20 feet on a side and is made from 1/2-inch diameter bars spaced 1/2 inch apart. A prison in the shape of a box can be up to 10 feet on a side, creating a solid barrier that prevents any matter from passing through it and blocking any spells cast into or out from the area. When you cast the spell, any creature that is completely inside the cage’s area is trapped. Creatures only partially within the area, or those too large to fit inside the area, are pushed away from the center of the area until they are completely outside the area. A creature inside the cage can’t leave it by nonmagical means. If the creature tries to use teleportation or interplanar travel to leave the cage, it must first make a Charisma saving throw. On a success, the creature can use that magic to exit the cage. On a failure, the creature can’t exit the cage and wastes the use of the spell or effect. The cage also extends into the Ethereal Plane, blocking ethereal travel. This spell can’t be dispelled by dispel magic.

No. Archivist Daysong believes more in the heart and joy of the people than the rule of law. The aspect of Roanoke that he will find will be the capstone of the lowly town pub. The pub is the unsung hero. It is a place of necessity and leisure. It is the foundation of every great adventure. Its doors will shelter its heros in laughter and lore. Its hearth will burn brightly in even the worst downpour. It will flow cleanly and chilled as a boon and a blessing to the inhabitants, even if all else in the city is corrupt. These walls will never fall so long as even one hero remains. Upon this foundation the mason begins to chisel these words “Never fast, Never thirst as you sit at this table. As you, here, uplift your cup.” In the lost language of the Brunelocks. Because he alone is the only person from the Old World who was invited to the New World, his powers are greatly strengthened by the four Wardens of Arcania. The balance of magic has shifted. And a local ley line (the Rose Line) causes the buildings to appear. First, a bridge spans the river. And then two halves of a small hamlet appear, arranged along ancient patterns of monolith construction. As the power fades, fractal patterns can be seen in the dirt.

my_ruling: Pukwudgie are passive until threatened. These gentle cousins to the troll are less aggressive but much better defended. When faced with possible combat, the Pukwudgie raises the quills on its body and spins around, smashing an opponent with its quill-covered tail. If out of range, of opponent, it uses a javelin. Size: Giant Armor Class 16 Hit Points (8d10+ 40) Speed 30 ft. ft. STR 18 (+4) DEX 13 (+1) CON 20 (+5) INT 7 (-2) WIS 9 (-1) CHA 7 (-2) Proficiency Bonus +3 Skills Perception +2 Senses darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12 Keen Smell: The Pukwudgie has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell. Ranged: Attack.The Pukwudgie makes one attacks: one with its Javelin. Ranged weapon (Piercing) range: 30/120 Melee Attack: Sticky Quill: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: (1d6 + 4) piercing damage. When the Pukwudgie strikes with its back, it dislodges 1d6 quills that automatically break off and lodge in the opponent’s flesh. A lodged quill imposes a –1 circumstance penalty to attacks, saves, and checks. Each 1 round thereafter, the quill moves deeper into the opponent’s flesh, dealing 1d2 additional points of damage. Removing the quill takes 1 full round and deals 1d4 additional points of damage. If the quill has been embedded for more than 10 rounds, a Strength check at DC 10 is needed to remove the quill. For every minute after that, the DC to remove a lodged quill increases by +1. An unarmed or melee touch attack against a Pukwudgie causes 1d4 quills to break off and lodge in the attacker.

As a Dm I know it is hard to plan one campaign for a few players, so the depth and cohesiveness of the world and game you put on each and every year for the number of players you do is Unbelievable. I can't imagine the workload behind the scenes for both you and the other DMs. But having seen you in chats and drawing late into the night for the weeks leading up to the game your sheer love and dedication to your world is evident. I can’t speak for others but I suspect this to be true for many, this game has been a lifeline to me through hard times, and has legitimately taught me how to live my life better. When I came into Roanoke in season 2 being nowhere near the origins of the game and knowing nobody I still felt welcome, but not only that the DMs and even other players treated me like a person instead of a kid. My appreciation for the time, thought, and work you have put into this game is unending. I really just want you to know how much this game and the work you have put in has done for me and to I'm sure so many others, it is beyond the scope of what any D&D game could be expected to do. Thank you always - Varn, Bekham, PC2, Josh

source_line: You contracted Sight Rot
my_ruling: This painful infection causes bleeding from the eyes and eventually blinds the Victim. A beast or Humanoid that drinks water tainted by sight rot must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become infected. One day after infection, the creature’s vision starts to become blurry. The creature takes a −1 penalty to Attack rolls and Ability Checks that rely on sight. At the end of each Long Rest after the symptoms appear, the penalty worsens by 1. When it reaches −5, the Victim is Blinded until its sight is restored by magic such as Lesser Restoration or heal.

my_ruling: Psychic Whispers. You can establish telepathic communication between yourself and others-perfect for quiet infiltration. As an action, choose one or more creatures you can see, up to a number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus, and then roll one Psionic Energy die. For a number of hours equal to the number rolled, the chosen creatures can speak telepathically with you, and you can speak telepathically with them. To send or receive a message (no action required), you and the other creature must be within 1 mile of each other. A creature can't use this telepathy if it can't speak any languages, and a creature can end the telepathic connection at any time (no action required). You and the creature don't need to speak a common language to understand each other. The first time you use this power after each long rest, you don't expend the Psionic Energy die. All other times you use the power, you expend the die.

my_ruling: A quick reminder about Rule 8 from the server rules: there can be times when we will step in to riff and improv on the things that catch our attention. There will be plenty of time to do what we call “Invitationals.” Invitationals are enacted when a player or a DM wants to follow through on an improv story line. They can be requested by anyone, but are fulfilled only as time and DM interest allows. Please remember that while for players this can feel like a big open sandbox game, the things in it that you are interacting with are people who donate their time. Its a big job that is as taxing as it is rewarding. Talk to you DMs about what you would like to accomplish in down time and invitationals. And when it works for them to help generate the hours and hours of content we provide (for free and on top of your jobs, lives and everything else.) We love you. Most of the DMs have not endured this gauntlet before. Trust me, trying to put this event on is one of the most challenging things a dm will ever do. Be patient courteous and kind to all of our volunteers. If a dm is running combat in voice, they might ask to keep mics closed when running. A very good habit to be in, is to pre type your action before your turn. Combat is long. You might have 20-30 minutes between rounds. Please do your best not to take extra time on your turn. It is a matter of kindness to your dms and courtesy to you fellow players. Remember to thank your mods, and listen to them when they mod combat and loot drops. Thanks -Radar.

my_ruling: Ah, meta gaming. That age old pastime of players. To the experienced player, it is the sharing of tricks of the trade and the fear of sub optimal playing. An experienced player will also relish the value of making intentionally unreliable or intentionally against the grain choices for role play reasons. But to the newer player, there comes a perceived pressure when their decisions are sub optimal. Wisdom is in being gentle enough with your opinions about how they should play, be it mechanics or social decisions. Personally, I often have a hard time reading social cues. And even then, lots of us have been playing together for years and ride that wave of emphatic group opinion. The number of neurodivergent players on the server is above half. And that is something to consider when it comes to interplay discussions about the how tos of role playing. Meta gaming and theory crafting about the plot is some of the most gratifying things a dm can read. But its is an acquired rhythm that becomes available as your become more experienced. There are lots of kick ass players on this server. There are also lots of people who love to protect and nurture those who could use it among us. Remember server rule 1. If you don't remember it, please take the time to reread it today. Its a big crazy day today. I hope you all have fun. XD

This doll attunes itself to you upon being picked up. While attuned to it and on your person, you gain a +1 to your AC and all saving throws. The stuffy acts as an Unseen Servant with the following changes, it has an AC of 13, 10 hit points, and a Strength of 10.The Sentinel Stuffy also has minimal sentience with an Intelligence of 4(-3), Wisdom of 10(+0), and a Charisma of 16(+3) It cannot speak, but understands all languages spoken by its owner. If you are separated from the Sentinel Stuffy for over 24hrs you will lose attunement, during this time the Stuffy will do all it can to get back to you.If you were to die due to overwhelming damage or from failing death saves, the Sentinel Stuffy takes your place when dying, becoming inanimate, and ending your attunement. Odd Heart Wondrous item (requires attunement) This item is one that has always been with you, your own heart, and its potential only unlocked by an experimental surgery. If you manage to survive the surgery you will awaken to your heart being encapsulated in a containment chamber of your own choosing and connected by a tubing or a cord to your chest. After the surgery you will find yourself permanently under the effect of Sanctuary(DC15) until you are unattuned. Whenever you roll a hit die you always take maximum healing. Once attuned to the Odd Heart you cannot unattune to it unless you die or undergo a more dangerous reversal surgery. Symbiotic Nature. The heart can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse or enter an anti-magic zone, your attunement to the heart ends, and you immediately fall unconscious and start making death saves. Phlogiston Pidgin Wondrous item (requires attunement) This prosthetic tongue was made with magi who have had their tongues forcibly removed. Taking a lump of molten phlogiston and molding it carefully, a person could replace their lost tongue. The extra dimensional energies inherent in the Phlogiston imbue the attuned with the languages of all the planes. While attuned you can cast Tongues on yourself a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus rounded down and resets on a long rest. You can also cast Speak with Animals, Plants, and Dead at will. You also gain proficiency in one of the following abilities: Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion. If you are already proficient in the chosen ability you gain expertise instead. Owl Feather Arrows Ammunition Fletched with feathers gifted by the Owl Folk of the Fae Wild, these arrows fly silently through the air avoiding nearly all detection. You can add your Wisdom modifier to your attack bonus when firing these arrows or bolts. When you fire one of these arrows or bolts from hiding, regardless if it hits, the intended target needs to make a perception check vs. your initial stealth check to detect you. If it misses the target makes the check with disadvantage and normally if it hits. If you are not detected you do not need to use the hide action again. When a rogue uses these arrows or bolts they get an extra 1d6 of Sneak Attack damage. Sea Farer's Foil (unique) common, wondrous rapier The blade is mounted on a hilt made of sea stone and carved to look like the body of a swordfish. Rumor has it that the piece of stone used was actually a piece of a Lodestone. While wielding this rapier and fighting underwater, you cannot receive disadvantage on attack rolls due to not having a swim speed.
